summary: Throughput & p95 spike from mixed short/long-sequence traffic causing KV-cache thrash on reserved pool
description: Customer reports sustained increase in p95 latency and frequent request timeouts (504) from their dedicated reserved pool in us-west-2 starting 2026-03-10 09:30 UTC. The pattern correlates with a sudden rise in mixed short (<=32 tokens) and long (>=1024 tokens) inference traffic. Symptoms: high queue depth, requests timing out at the gateway, and several backend 5xx errors. Customer uses pinned model redwood-rlhf-1 for chat and gptj-6b for background scoring. They see degraded throughput (~40% drop) and elevated tail latency during bursts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send interleaved traffic: 60% short seq (<=32 tokens) chat calls at QPS 150 and 40% long seq (>1024 tokens) at QPS 30 to the customer's reserved pool endpoint.
2) Observe request queue length and p95 in Grafana (serving-runtime -> request_queue_depth, p95_latency).
3) Reproduce during peak autoscaler window (03:30-10:30 PDT) where the reservation had recent scale-in activity.
logs: kibana: 2026-03-10T09:31:12Z WARN serving-runtime request queued due to KV cache miss and cache invalidation lock (trace request_id=953a2f)
kube-events: 2026-03-10T09:29Z Node nv-3 preempted background batch pods, ephemeral OOM kills observed on batch-worker-7
gateway logs: repeated 504s for route /v1/generate with upstream timeout after 20s
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: mixed short/long sequences cause repeated KV-cache churn and frequent cache invalidation which increases CPU/GPU host-side lock contention and per-request setup time.
Observed autoscaler behavior: recent scale-in at 2026-03-10T08:45Z reduced capacity by 1 GPU slice; scale-up latency ~90s which allowed burst to overload remaining workers.
Noisy neighbor: background embedding batch jobs from a different tenant were scheduled to same node group; kube evictions and memory pressure spikes coincide with p95 increases.
Serving runtime traces show per-request host-copy time increased by ~3x during the window; KV cache hit-rate dropped from 92% to 48%.
Gateway retries were disabled for this customer's route; lack of short-retry made timeouts visible to the customer.
Related metrics and dashboards linked: grafana panels + trace ids.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:05 - Priya Shah: Customer confirms impact started after they rolled out a new scoring job that interleaves short/long requests. They are blocking with production traffic.
2026-03-10 10:20 - Liam O'Connor: Assigned to investigate scheduler placement and autoscaler thresholds. Kicking off dedicated pool live-debug with SRE.
2026-03-10 11:00 - SRE (internal): Found batch-worker pods scheduled onto reserved nodes; suggested tainting reserved nodes to prevent background batch placement until remediation.

2026-03-11 02:30 - Liam O'Connor: Temporary mitigation applied: tainted reserved node group to prevent batch scheduling and raised autoscaler min capacity by 1 slice for the customer's reservation (manual override). Observed p95 drop back to baseline over 15 minutes.
2026-03-12 09:00 - Customer (Nimbus): Confirmed throughput recovered and timeouts stopped after mitigation; requesting root cause and permanent fix.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: tainted reserved nodes to prevent background batch pods and manually increased reservation min capacity to avoid autoscale undershoot. Root cause appears to be a combination of KV-cache thrashing driven by mixed short/long sequence patterns and background batch jobs colocated on reserved nodes; autoscaler scale-in removed one critical slice making the pool brittle to bursts. Next steps: revert taint after deploy of scheduler fix, implement autoscaler hysteresis for reserved pools, add isolation policy to scheduler to avoid placing background batch pods on reserved nodes, and add a short-retry policy for customer gateway routes. Follow-up ticket created for permanent changes.
